goal: Create an illustrative hackathon judging advert for the current TaskGoblin prototype without recorded product footage.
prompt: Create a polished 90-second illustrated product advert for TaskGoblin, a Telegram-native AI project manager. Use stylised Telegram-like conversations, animated task cards, project-memory diagrams, confirmation buttons, document icons, reminders, and a dark TaskGoblin dashboard rather than recorded product footage. Open with useful commitments disappearing inside a noisy group chat. Show TaskGoblin noticing a concrete assignment, resolving the owner only from known group members, checking project context, and creating a reviewable candidate. Make the safety boundary visible: most consequential AI suggestions wait for human confirmation. When a member explicitly completes a confidently matched task, TaskGoblin updates it through a controlled workflow, transfers ownership to the person who completed it, and reacts to the source message with a green check. Show /undo reversing the latest mistaken task change. Show the daily 8pm Singapore project report with progress, urgent work, blockers, owners and a seven-day outlook. Show current capabilities only: group onboarding, member linking, task proposals, assignments, progress, completion, deadline, blocker and decision detection; multi-task proposal batches; PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD project context; private Telegram reminders; /start, /help, /summary, /project, /kpi, /tasks, /mytasks and /undo; Telegram web login; project dashboard; list, Kanban and calendar views; and authorised task creation and editing. Do not show /recent, /addtask, /done, /update, /setproject or /addmilestone. Do not present TaskGoblin as an autonomous coding agent. Use an evidence-led hackathon tone: focused, intelligent, trustworthy and lightly playful. Finish with the line 'Turn conversation into accountable project memory' and the URL 'taskgoblin.vercel.app'.

narration.script: Project work already happens in chat. Someone accepts a task, a deadline changes, a blocker appears—and moments later, the commitment is buried beneath the conversation. TaskGoblin turns permitted Telegram group messages into persistent project memory. It detects high-signal events such as proposals, assignments, progress, completions, deadlines, blockers and decisions. Most consequential suggestions remain reviewable: TaskGoblin checks known members, existing tasks, recent context and likely duplicates, preserves the source message, then asks the team to confirm. Explicit completion is faster. When a confidently matched task is finished, TaskGoblin reacts with a green check, marks it complete, and records the member who actually did the work as its owner. If the latest task change was wrong, slash undo restores the previous state. Share a PDF, Word document, text file or Markdown brief, and TaskGoblin uses its extracted content as bounded project context. It can propose several tasks, send private deadline reminders, and answer grounded follow-ups. Every day at eight PM Singapore time, the project group receives a report showing progress, urgent work, blockers, ownership and the next seven days. Confirmed information also appears in a Telegram-authenticated dashboard with editable tasks, project health, a Kanban board and a calendar. TaskGoblin keeps humans in control while turning conversation into accountable project memory.

scenes.visuals: A busy illustrated Telegram-like group chat fills the frame. Important messages such as 'I will build the API' and 'Due Friday' are pushed upward by jokes and acknowledgements.
onScreenText: PROJECT WORK ALREADY HAPPENS IN CHAT
scenes.transition: A neon green thread catches the disappearing commitment.

scenes.visuals: The green thread guides one source message into a structured event card. Small context tiles appear for known members, existing tasks, recent messages and duplicates.
scenes.transition: The event card pauses before a confirmation gate.

scenes.purpose: Explain confirmation, completion attribution and undo.
scenes.visuals: A source-linked candidate card displays concise rationale and confidence. Confirm and Ignore controls appear for an inferred assignment. Beside it, an explicit completion message receives a green check reaction; its task moves to Done and the owner changes to the member who completed it. A quick /undo restores the earlier state.
onScreenText: REVIEW WHEN AMBIGUOUS. UPDATE WHEN EXPLICIT.
scenes.transition: A confirmed card clicks into the project-memory timeline.

scenes.purpose: Show document context and multi-task planning.
scenes.visuals: PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD pages feed a bounded context panel. One planning request unfolds into several reviewable task cards instead of one oversized task.
onScreenText: PROJECT CONTEXT, NOT JUST ONE MESSAGE
scenes.transition: Task cards fan into Telegram and the dashboard.

scenes.visuals: Animate group onboarding, member linking, a concise /summary response, an interactive /tasks selection, a private deadline reminder, and an 8pm group report covering urgent work, ownership, progress and the next seven days.
scenes.transition: A dashboard link expands into the website.

scenes.purpose: Show the web correction and overview surface.
scenes.visuals: A dark TaskGoblin dashboard appears after Telegram login. Move a task across a Kanban board, edit its owner and deadline, then switch to a calendar view.
onScreenText: Kanban • Calendar • Editable tasks • Project health
scenes.transition: The dashboard zooms out into a simple system diagram.

scenes.purpose: Communicate engineering credibility without invented metrics.
scenes.visuals: A clean pipeline shows Telegram webhook, deterministic routing, OpenAI Structured Outputs, persisted candidates, Supabase state and human confirmation. A test grid illuminates behind it.
onScreenText: Structured outputs • Source traceability • 100+ automated tests
scenes.transition: All elements collapse into the TaskGoblin mark.

scenes.purpose: Deliver the product promise and call to action.
scenes.visuals: TaskGoblin logo on the dark green canvas with a soft acid-lime glow. A final chat bubble becomes a checked task card.
onScreenText: TURN CONVERSATION INTO ACCOUNTABLE PROJECT MEMORY
scenes.transition: Hold the final card for two seconds.
